title: Vision-Based Driver's Cognitive Load Classification Considering Eye Movement Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning.
summary: With 33 male drivers in a simulator, eye-movement features supported SVM classification of task-induced cognitive-load labels at 92% accuracy (CNN: 91%); this is an experimental driver-monitoring result, not clinical or road-safety validation.
ai_technology: Eye-movement signals/features from a camera and eye tracker fed ML/DL classifiers; Methods §§2.1–2.4.
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: Experimental Results §3.4 reports SVM 92% and CNN 91% classification accuracy for induced cognitive-load classes.
evidence.unknown: Only 33 male participants in a simulator; evaluation is within this recruited sample and does not establish performance on real roads or broader driver populations.
evidence.ai_role: Eye-movement signals/features from a camera and eye tracker fed ML/DL classifiers; Methods §§2.1–2.4.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
